The suspected thugs are reported to have hijacked a matatu but were intercepted by detectives from the Special Crime Prevention Unit (SCPU), who were trailing the gangsters from Githurai.

A Seventh Day Adventist pastor was killed by suspected sungu sungu gangsters in Nyamira County at the weekend. Neighbors said that the attackers, who allegedly posed as uniformed security officers, attacked the home at 8pm and killed Mr. Orina.

A bomb exploded on a bus in central Nairobi Monday during a security search before it left for Kampala, killing three and wounding 23. An official with Kampala Coach Ltd said the would-be attacker was among those wounded or killed by the blast.

The protesters, waving placards and chanting slogans against substance abuse, were confronted by a gang of youths who reportedly pelted them with stones next to the Kisauni CDF offices.

Mystery surrounds the death of a prominent Machakos businessman after a post-mortem examination revealed a gun shot wound in the head. Mr Abed Makau Kikuyu, the proprietor of Tea Tot Hotels, was found dead at the Haile Selassie Road roundabout in Nairobi on the morning of December 31.
A British tourist and Kenyan companion were seized night in a carjacking ordeal on Mombasa Road, Nairobi. They were later helped to escape by villagers near the kidnappers den in Kiambu.

Unknown assailants ambushed a Nairobi top cop on Saturday night and shot him thrice before making away with his firearm. Shauri Moyo deputy OCS Inspector John Marete was shot on the neck and stomach in Nairobis Majengo area at around 9pm.

A Rwandese working for the World Bank was also shot at the gate of his residence in Mimosa Court on early Sunday. The official was confronted by armed thugs who robbed him of his valuables before shooting him on the thigh. They drove away with his Toyota Landcruiser.

However, the intruders were overpowered and thrown out of the rally as residents who stood at a distance cheered.

Eight people were struck by bullets fired by militiamen who have been fighting AU troops on the Somalia side. One Kenyan woman was killed.

Unidentified men riding in a taxi hurled a hand grenade at a police vehicle passing by the Nairobi Hotel in Mandera's main market in the evening of 05/09. The group then directed small arms fire at the police, forcing the police to withdraw quickly, before their damaged vehicle broke down along the road to the police station.  Three police officers and a civilian (a cashier at the Nairobi Hotel) were injured in the attack.  The attackers managed to escape the scene without suffering any casualties.
A device suspected to be an IED exploded in front of the Central AP camp in Mandera in the evening of 05/09. No casualties were reported.
Three people were shot dead when armed assailants of Somali origin attacked a remote village in Malalani location, Kitui East constituency. The violence may have escalated from an argument.
Six people were injured after they were attacked in a suspected land control disagreement.
An attorney defending the Bungoma area Senator is assassinated for suspected political reasons.

Police sentries in the main Mandera Police Line reportedly opened fire in the night of 27/09. The reason behind the shooting is unclear. Reports indicate that although police claim to have been fired upon, there is no evidence that an attack took place.

A prominent cleric and three others are assassinated outside Mombasa. The reason for the attack is not known. The following day a group of locals renewed a protest against the murder, which became violent. Some accusations held the police were involved in the assassination, though they have denied any involvement.
An unknown group attacked a Giriama village near Kipini in the Tana River Delta, burning three homes.
A group of police who were returning from patrol opened fire on a group of men planting an IED along the side of the road the night of 11/10. The police failed to hit or capture any of the men.
A young boy is killed and three others injured after a landmine detonated in Mandera border town. The group many have been playing with the mine, not aware that it was dangerous.
A man is shot and killed with arrows along the on the Chemelil-Nandi border. The reason for the attack is not known.
A Christian church leader is murdered late in the evening by unknown assailants.
A Christian church leader is murdered by unknown assailants.

Political separatists of the Mombasa Republican Council (MRC) attack a police post in Palakumi, Kilifi, injuring one officer. According to Kilifi County AP Commandant Elijah Ngetich, 10 suspected MRC militants, armed with arrows and bows, carried out the midnight raid at Palakumi in Ganze. The motive has not been established although some claim they were out to steal weapons.

Three people were shot dead after youths armed with arrows attacked Ruga police post in Muhoroni Sub County. The three are reported to have been shot dead in an arrow and fire exchange at Nyangore sub-location in Chemelil. The youths are suspected to have come from Nandi community. The youths had vowed to kill a senior police officer, accusing police of contributing to the rampant chaos along the nearby border area.
A police officer is shot twice, in the head and back, by two unknown gunmen on a motorcycle at around 8.30pm at Afisi ya Kanu stage in Mwandoni Ndogo.

An unidentified gunmen is killed and a police officer is wounded after the gunmen launched an attack in the Lexington area of Nairobi. The motive for the attack is not known.
An unidentified man hacks a woman to death in a land dispute.
A Red Cross officer is shot and injured by an armed group after delivering supplies to Nakwamoru village.
Two men were in the evening hours shot dead at Kasses village in West Pokot by suspected raiders.

A group of "radical Muslim youths" raid a mosque attempting to attack the resident imam, who was inside delivering a sermon. Inside, a group of youths came to the defence of the imam, clashing with the intruders. Several reported injuries reported as result of the clash. Police later arrived to disperse the warring sides.

Two General Service Unit officers (paramilitary wing of the Kenyan Military) were injured when a vehicle they were travelling in was attacked in West Pokot county. The attackers may have been thieves.
An unidentified person threw a hand grenade into a group of British tourists in the Likoni area of Mombasa. The grenade failed to explode.
The bodies to two men are discovered in Kilifi, having been shot at close range. The attackers and their motivations are not known.

Two people were killed and at least three others injured in two explosions targeting police officers in the north-eastern Kenyan town of Wajir. The explosions took place near the Baraza park in the town. The injured were taken to Wajir general hospital. Reports say there have been several arrests in connection with the explosions.

A Muslim cleric has been shot dead by two gunmen at Kona ya Musa in Diani, Kwale county. The cleric was shot in the head unknown people a few metres from his business some minutes after evening prayers on 18/12.
At least two people were shot dead, and four others injured in a gun attack in Wajir town. This is the second attack in a week. A gunman shot the victims indiscriminately before escaping.
A group of youths, suspected to be members or supports of the MRC petrol bomb two churches during the early morning hours. Causalities not known.
A prominent cleric is shot and killed in Ukunda, his killers escaped by motorbike. According to police reports the cleric was specifically targeted.

An explosive device believed to be an IED targeted a police vehicle in the vicinity of Juba Primary School in Dagahley Camp in Dadaab District in the morning of 30/12. The police vehicle was escorting an NGO vehicle carrying out borehole refuelling. One police officer was reportedly injured by the explosion. The vehicle was severely damaged.

A Kenya police reservist was shot dead by unidentified armed raiders in a fresh attack at Turkwel on Pokot-Turkana border. The police officer of the Turkana ethnic group, though it was not clear if ethnicity was the motive for the attack.

At least ten are injured in a grenade attack at a nightclub in Diani, 25km outside of Mombasa. The attack occurred around 4am. Witnesses claim they saw an individual lob the explosive into a group of people, though the person's identity remain unknown. The target of the blast may have been a group of British tourists present in the bar.
A hand grenade is thrown at a police officer in the Diani area. The ordinance did not explode. The perpetrators escaped.
A hand grenade is thrown at a police vehicle in Ukunda. The five officers present escaped unhurt.

An unknown number of people are feared dead and several others injured in Marsabit following fresh attacks by bandits believed to be from Ethiopia. The attack comes just days after four people were killed in the relative area over a water hole dispute, though it is not clear if this attack was motivated by ethnicity.

Three IEDs were detonated in the vicinity of firewood distribution centre in IFO 1 (Dadaab District) in the morning of 08/12. Reports indicate that the first explosion targeted the rear police escort vehicle of the regular morning convoy to IFO 1 and Dagahaley. The second set targeted the police responders, of whom a number had by then arrived at the scene. No one was injured by any of the blasts. The police vehicle initially targeted by the perpetrators only sustained slight damages. There were gunshots fired by the police after the second explosion. One man was injured in its aftermath, trampled by a panicked crowd running from the scene.
Unidentified gunmen open fire on Bungoma senator-elect Moses Wetang'ula's car during the evening hours along Mbagathi Way. The Senator escaped unhurt.

Unidentified militia, believed to be from nearby Ethiopia attack the ethnic Gabra border town of North Horr, killing two police and injuring "scores" of civilians. It was reported cattle was stolen in the raid.

A senior Mijikenda Kayak elder was shot dead by unknown gangsters during the evening hours at his home in Jamb area of Wartime. Family members said the man had no local grudges and they had no idea of the motive.

A blast of unknown origin occurs at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport during the evening hours. The body of a Somali national was later discovered, however his causes of death is believed to be from gunfire. Nevertheless, authorities believe his death is related to the blast perpetrators. The  following three days several arrests were made.

The more than 200 youth, armed with weapons raided a sand harvesting site in Kedong Ranch and set the lorries ablaze. The attack follows a fall-out between traders and the youth from Mai Mahiu over control of the sand business.
A bomb was in the early morning hurled at a primary school in Likoni, Mombasa. Police say the device exploded inside the school compound, but no injuries have been reported.

A group of men from Kericho West attacked Nyakach during the overnight hours in revenge over stolen cattle. Several houses were torched, leaving many displaced and homeless. No report of death or injury. The exact date of the raid is not clear.

A man is killed in Taveta following fighting over a land dispute. Witnesses said the deceased, who is the land owner, had gone to mark the boundary of their land at Makongeni area when they were attacked by unknown assailants.

Makueni MP Daniel Maanzo and his wife are admitted at the Nairobi hospital after they were attacked and injured by armed thugs at their home. The attackers also stole cash and other valuables. It is not clear if the attack had political motivations.

Three people were injured after a gang of about 10 people attacked worshipers at a church in Bamburi's Mwembe Legeza area in Mombasa during the morning hours morning. The reason for the attack is not clear.

Six people were injured during a confrontation between farmers and pastoralists at Mtondoni area in Hongwe ward, Lamu West district. The conflict ensued when pastoralists were accused of driving their animals into the farms and destroying crops. The identities of the two groups is not known.

Attackers with guns and explosives raided a jail in a restive Nigerian city on Sunday, leaving four Prison Guards dead and freeing 40 inmates. Boko Haram is blamed. The gunmen also attacked a school in the town.

Gunmen with explosives attacked a police station on Tuesday in the northern Nigerian city of Kano, previously targeted by Islamist militant group Boko Haram. The clash lasted into a second day, resulting in the death of seventeen militants and one police officer.
Gunmen attack a police post, no report of death of injury.
Day two of attacks on a police station by suspected Boko Haram. Seventeen militants and one police officer killed by the end of the battle. Several arrested.
Unidentified Gunmen attack a police station, two civilians, two insurgents killed. Several other police stations were attacked in the metro area in an apparent coordinated effort.
Gunmen suspected to be Boko Haram attack a police station and a bank in a small town. "Many lives" were said to have been lost in the attack.

EVENT_TYPE: Non-violent activity by a conflict actor
NOTES: Explosives were found planted at a police station and filling station, but were detonated by a local bomb squad before they were able to cause damage.
Gunmen have killed the Rivers State Chairman of the All Nigeria Peoples Party, Mr. Julius Nwaofu. He was shot several times after leaving the airport. Assailants unknown.

Police say security forces have killed suspected sect members during a military raid on their hideout in a besieged city in Nigeria's northeast. The police were not clear with regard to the number of deceased.
Gunmen entered Kurna Asabe area of Kano metropolis and killed a former local government councilor, a woman and a teenager. The Politian's political party was not mentioned.

EVENT_TYPE: Non-violent activity by a conflict actor
NOTES: Following a tip, police discover a pair of bombs placed by unknown persons. The bomb squad detonated to bombs before they were able to cause damage.

An Improvised Explosive Device (IED) exploded on under a bridge near a village in the Riyom Local Government of Plateau State, north-central Nigeria, just as the police detonated two more bombs planted in the same area, some 40 kilometers from Jos, the state capital. No word of causalities. Riyom has witnessed some bomb blasts and constant rifts between members of the Berom ethnic group and Fulani herdsmen, though there is no word who is responsible here.

Gunfire and explosions rocked the northeastern Nigerian city of Damaturu on Saturday as security forces launched a pre-emptive offensive against Boko Haram Islamists. The offensive followed intelligence that BH was planning to launch an attack on the city. The violence was most heavily concentrated in the Nyanya and Obasanjo Estates areas of the city.
Unidentified gunmen have shot and killed two people leaving one other person critically injured when the struck at Gwandu quarters of Shamaki ward in Gombe metropolis.
Military forces shoot and kill three suspected Boko Haram members. One female was arrested.
Boko Haram attackers killed nine construction workers in the restive northeastern city of Maiduguri, the base of the Islamist sect.
An explosion that went off near a shopping mall in Nigeria's capital causing one injury.

Suspected gunmen believed to be members of the Boko Haram sect attacked the Borno State Housing Corporation (BOHC) office complex in Maiduguri, killing its General Manager, Isa Madu Ngaram and an engineer.

EVENT_TYPE: Non-violent activity by a conflict actor
NOTES: Police discover and detonate a pair of explosives in the Congo Russia neighborhood of the city. It is unknown who the perpetrators are, however, the police force publically blamed Boko Haram.
Military forces raid a Boko Haram hideout, kill one member of the sect.
Suspected Boko Haram attack a Damaturu slum with explosives and firearms. Causalities and damage unknown.

Suspected members of Boko Haram attacked the residence of an Islamic cleric, Shehu of Borno, Alhaji Abubakar Umar Garbai El-Kanem, killing a resident of the palace as well as a trader in a nearby market.
Suspected members of Boko Haram attack and kill an Islamic cleric, Sheikh Ibrahim Majimi, at his home.
Unknown gunmen kill four, injure one.
Reports of two small villages attacked by unknown people in Plateau State. Over 140 dead. The military disputes this claim.
Reports of two small villages attacked by unknown people in Plateau State. Over 140 dead. The military disputes this claim.

A suicide bomber kills 10 in a Mosque near the Shehu's palace. The Shehu is the top Islamic leader in the state. Six others injured. The bomber was a teenage boy, whom security experts believe was involved with Boko Haram.
Unidentified gunmen attack and kill a Divisional Police Officer for unknown reasons.
Gunmen, suspected to be Boko Haram, attack a small town outside Kaduna, kill one.
A bomb is detonated in a car outside a church during Sunday services, no causalities. Police arrest two suspects following the incident, who are believed to be involved in Boko Haram.

EVENT_TYPE: Non-violent activity by a conflict actor
NOTES: Heavy gunfire reported in the Yobe State capital. Suspected Boko Haram members raid a police station. The organization later claims credit for the attack.
When a grenade is thrown at a Islamic school in a Jos suburb security agents respond with gunfire. One small boy was killed by the blast.
An explosion outside a government building kills at least one. It is unknown is perpetrated the incident, though it is believed to be either Boko Haram or a Fulani group.

EVENT_TYPE: Non-violent activity by a conflict actor
NOTES: Hotel staff discover an unexploded bomb. Boko Haram is suspected.
Boko Haram attacks a JTF team along a road. Unknown causalities.
Gunmen, suspected to be of Boko Haram, target Ibo Christians in an open air market and kill four.

EVENT_TYPE: Non-violent activity by a conflict actor
NOTES: Police forces discover an explosives outside a Catholic school in the capital and dispose of it before it is able to detonate.
Six are dead, including a police constable when gunmen on motorcycles attack a market area. Boko Haram is widely believed to be responsible.
Gunmen, suspected to be linked to Boko Haram attack a radio station and kill three. Sharada is a Kano neighborhood south east of the downtown area.
A gunman attacks a regional leader of MASSOB, but the leader escapes unharmed. It is unclear if this was an assassination attempt or a robbery.

Boko Haram kills a 10-yesr-old boy and wounds 10 others. The explosion occurred in the city's Tundunwadan Dan-iya area, a nightlife and pub district, a common target of Boko Haram, who later clamed credit for the blast.

Unidentified gunmen shot dead a Health Ministry worker after he was followed. The reasons for the killing are unknown. Witnesses claim the assailants did not leave the scene of the crime until they knew the victim was dead.
A prominent Christian leader is killed, his wife abducted, after unidentified gunmen storm their church.
Armed men of the Boko Haram sect attacked a police station, set it ablaze. It is suspected these are the same gunmen involved in the attack in rural Bauchi State
Following the killing of two Indians, members of Boko Haram attacked a police station in a separate attack in a different area of the city. Two police and civilian shot dead in the attack.
Two Indian nationals are killed in a suspected Boko Haram attack on their factory. Other were injured.
Suspected Boko Haram gunmen attack a police station. Three police reported killed.
Shortly after Boko Haram killed two Indian nationals in a factory, the JTF makes 26 BH arrests and kills two in a raid.
On motorcycles, suspected Boko Haram assassinate a senior member of the police forces while he ate at home. Three of the officer's guests were also shot and killed.
The traditional ruler of an area is kidnapped by unknown men, later released.

Boko Haram attackers opened fire on Mosque worshippers. Three of the gunmen were shot by police who were present to protest the worshipers, while a fourth was killed when the explosive device he was carrying went off prematurely. Conflicting reports have the death count at five.

Motorcycle gunmen, suspected to be Boko Haram, opened fire on the car of a senior Nigerian air force officer Sunday, killing the driver and an aide (both junior air force officers), but the senior officer was not inside the vehicle at the time. Two pedestrians were collateral damage.

Gunmen on motorcycles attacked the country home of the Nigerian Vice President. The Vice President was not in the residence at the time, though one civilian was killed. Boko Haram later claimed credit for the attack. Two of the three perpetrators arrested.

Explosions, including a suicide blast, rocked two police stations in Nigeria's northwestern city of Sokoto. Boko Haram later claims credit. Six killed, including civilians, 30 other's injured. Other reports have the death count at four, others three.

Nigerian troops kill two members of Boko Haram new the country's border with Chad. The alleged insurgents were caught carrying rocket-propelled grenades, Kalashnikov rifles as well as other assorted ammunition and weaponry.

EVENT_TYPE: Non-violent activity by a conflict actor
NOTES: Police discover and dispose of a explosive found at a school. Boko Haram is suspected, but there is no evidence to support the claim.
Boko Haram attacks a second police station into another area of the city, in an apparent coordinated attack.

Suspected Boko Haram simultaneously attacked two police stations in Gombe. "They threw explosives and opened fire on the police post in central Gombe. Some of the policeman were inside while others were outside. The explosions were followed by gunfire. There was a shootout between the gunmen and policemen which lasted till 10 pm (2100 GMT)," a witness said. "There were a lot of gunshots lasting for more than an hour. I cannot say if anybody was hurt or killed in the attack," he continued.
Report of a bomb explosion at a church. However, conflicting accounts report no explosion at all.

A Muslim leader escaped a suicide attack in a mosque by suspected Boko Haram, who later claimed credit . "The bomber, however, detonated the explosives and blew himself off, injuring two policemen and three civilians in the process," a local official said.
Boko Haram attacks a third neighborhood in Maiduguri.

Boko Haram detonated explosions in three neighborhoods in Maiduguri. Following the violence soldiers went door-to-door arresting suspects. Some residents report unneeded violence at the hands of the soldiers. No reported death or injury.
Boko Haram attacks a second neighborhood in Maiduguri.

Unidentified gunmen attacked a oil vessel off the coast of Nigeria, killing two sailors and kidnapping four others. The victims were not citizens of Nigeria. Following the event the Nigerian military launched efforts to recover the victims.

A suicide bomber rammed his car into a military patrol in the northeastern Nigerian city of Damaturu, killing himself, six soldiers, and two civilians. Boko Haram was suspected and later claimed responsibility. Nine other were hospitalized.
Rival "cult" groups clash over the course of two days, causing at least tow deaths and other injuries.
Rival "cult" groups clash over the course of two days, causing at least tow deaths and other injuries.
Suspected Boko Haram opens fire on a crowded church during an evening service, at least 19 dead. Unknown injury number.
Day two of rival cult clash.
Day two of rival cult clash.

Unknown assailants opened fire on a group of soldiers on patrol, sparking an exchange of fire that left two soldiers and two of the gunmen dead. It is unclear if the perpetrators have any connection to the church attackers the previous night.
Suspected members of Boko Haram kill two police officers along a rural road.

Members and adherents of the BSDF declare their independence from Nigeria, believing the land of southeast Cross River State rightfully belongs to Cameroon. Upen their declaration the group launched a radio station.
Unidentified gunmen attack a church, set it ablaze. Injuries, one death reported.
Suspected Boko Haram kill one member of a security forces and wound two others in a "terrorist attack."

Joint Task Force (military force) killed 20 suspected Boko Haram members in a shootout as they raided their hideout in Maiduguri. Conflicting report: some accounts have this event occurring on the 13th of the month.
Gunmen, suspected to be members of Boko Haram attack a church in Gombe.
A JTF raid on two Boko Haram hideouts results in the death of two militants and the arrest of 30 others. Panicked residents flee the city in large numbers.
A JTF raid on two Boko Haram hideouts results in the death of two militants and the arrest of 30 others. Panicked residents flee the city in large numbers.
A gang known as the Area Boys attacks a journalist.
Six unidentified men attack journalists on a train.

Three people were killed in a bomb blast on a northern Nigerian road leading to a mosque where a cleric had condemned the Islamist militant group Boko Haram. The ordinance was delivered on motorcycle.

Two suspected suicide bombers were killed by an Improvised Explosive Device (IED) while another person suspected to be a member of the group escaped with injuries. Their bomb was concealed in a camera case. The assailants were unknown, but it is likely they were members of Boko Haram. Some reports have the death count at three.
A Boko Haram suicide bomber killed himself and a civilian while wounding three others in an attack targeting a military vehicle. The members of the military were not harmed.
Military forces battle Boko Haram when they raid their hideout. 30 arrested.
A gun duel between Boko Haram and JTF security forces lasts two hours. One militant death reported, one soldier injured.
Gunmen, suspected to be Boko Haram, attack a mosque and shot dead a member of the Borno Emirate Traditional Council (BETC), Zanna Kaselama.
Hundreds evacuate a downtown building after a bomb scare.
During a Muslim celebration festival unknown persons bomb a police station. The blast injured one person and destroyed property.

Violence broke out at the Rivers State University of Science and Technology (RSUST) as "hoodlums" attacked officials of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) opposed to the appointment of an acting vice chancellor.
An unidentified gunman is killed after a three hour gun battle with police.
After a suspected Boko Haram attack in their neighborhood, a group of Christian youths seek revenge on their attackers. Police we able to foil most of the violence.

A policeman was reportedly injured when suspected Boko Haram members fired at a military roadblock along Maiduguri Road, Kano, while the police stopped a violent confrontation between Boko Haram and some residents of the area. Many cars damaged.
Suspected Boko Haram militants disrupt a Eid-el-Fitr celebration, no report of death or injury.
Boko Haram suspects attack a Christian church and a school. No report of injury or death. It is believed this group is the same group that attacked the police station elsewhere in the city.
Boko Haram suspects open fire on separate mosques, killing two.

Boko Haram suspects attack a police station/prison and exchange gunfire. Reports of civilian injury or death, though numbers are unknown The gun battle lasted at least two hours according to witnesses.
Two suspected assassins are killed in a police gun battle. The two are believed to be in connection with the death of a British national.
Boko Haram gunmen (suspected) shoot and kill a Irish national working for a construction firm.
Unidentified gunmen invaded Okordia community in Yenagoa Local Government Area, Bayelsa State, and abducted a clan head, or traditional ruler at a local palace.
Unidentified gunmen follow a police officer into a Mosque, kill him.
Unidentified gunmen abduct a government official.
A group of armed men, believed to be Boko Haram, shoot and kill a police officer during a gun battle.

Suspected Boko Haram detonated an explosive in the Gwange area of the city late in the afternoon. Sporadic gunshots were reported in the area soon after. There was a explosion earlier in the day elsewhere in the city.
Suspected Boko Haram suicide bomber was killed as well as a passerby when his explosive detonated prematurely. The suspected target was members of the JTF.

Suspected members of Boko Haram attempt to bomb a JTF patrol, but the device exploded prematurely destroying nearby shops. Members of the JTF react with gunfire costing five members of BH their lives.
A group of suspected Boko Haram ambushed a JTF patrol, though the counterattack killed all five attackers.
Suspected Boko Haram attacked a military checkpoint, kill an intelligence officer.
A JTF patrol is ambushed by members of Boko Haram. One officer was reported killed.

Gunmen suspected to be members of the Boko Haram, weekend, stormed New Marte, Marte Local Government Area of Borno State, where they killed a Police Sergeant (names withheld), and two civilians. The group also burnt a police headquarters and a local church.
Six are shot dead by suspected Boko Haram. The event may have occurred on 2nd September.
Suspected Boko Haram kills a man in Gwange Ward of the city.
Suspected Boko Haram kills a man in Ummarari Ward of the city.
Boko Haram members detonated a bomb in the Sabon neighborhood of Gombe. No causalities confirmed.

A local government secretary of Bama Council area of Borno state, and his friend, a university lecturer were shot dead by gunmen suspected to be Boko Haram in the same area where six people were shot and killed by the same group on Saturday.
Unknown gunmen burnt the personal house of Damaturu local government PDP chairman Alhaji Audu
Unidentified men attempt to attack three police vehicles with explosives, but are unsuccessful.
Boko Haram carries out a series of coordinated attacked on telecommunications facilities in several areas. One is injured at this location, while several others ran for safety following the blast.
Boko Haram carries out a series of coordinated attacked on telecommunications facilities in several areas. Two bombs failed to detonate in tow separate areas along Gombe road.
Men believed to be of Boko Haram attacked a home and killed four Igbos. It is unclear if the group was targeted because they were Igbos or if the attack was coincidental.
Boko Haram attack several telecommunication offices in a small geographic area. No report of injury or death.

Boko Haram set ablaze a telecommunications office in a coordinated effort to destroy much of the area's infrastructure. Sources revealed that the assailants, who were about 10 in number, stormed the telecommunications office around 2a.m. Wednesday and chased away the security men on duty before setting the building on fire.
Boko Haram attack several telecommunication offices in a small geographic area. No report of injury or death.

EVENT_TYPE: Non-violent activity by a conflict actor
NOTES: Men on motorbikes, believed to be Boko Haram, destroyed MTN and Airtel mobil phone telecommunication masts during the early morning hours.

Suspected Boko Haram attacked two buildings housing the Ministry of Religious Affairs and the state's Pilgrims Welfare Commission (YPWC) located on Potiskum Road. There was no official confirmation of the casualty figures but hospital sources claimed that 16 bodies were brought to the facility by the police and the JTF. The attacked carried into the early hours of the following day.
An attack on a JTF patrol results in a counterattack and the death of seven Boko Haram attackers. 13 others arrested.
Boko Haram continuers their attacks on telecommunication offices.
Unidentified gunmen disrupt a political meeting.
The Military's Operation Restore Order shoots and kills seven suspected members of Boko Haram and arrested 13 others during a raid operation.
Boko Haram's attacks on telecommunication offices continue, many buildings in the area set ablaze.
Military officials kill seven suspected members of Boko Haram at a military checkpoint. 13 others arrested. No casualty was recorded on the part of the soldiers

EVENT_TYPE: Non-violent activity by a conflict actor
NOTES: A JTF task force raid a Boko Haram hideout, arrest five members.

EVENT_TYPE: Non-violent activity by a conflict actor
NOTES: Nigerian forces arrest 11 members of Boko Haram and recover weapons.
Following a gunfight, the JTF arrested six suspects of a recent kidnapping of a university lecturer.
Unidentified gunmen attacked the home of a member of the Federal House of Representatives (name withheld), killing a young boy in the process.

Gunmen suspected of belonging to the Boko Haram Islamist sect late Sunday shot dead at least six people who were playing ludo game in northern Nigerian city of Bauchi. Conflicting reports have the death total at 5.
Gunmen kill a security officer and three members of his family. Authorities believe Boko Haram is responsible.
Gunmen shot dead the acting Chairman of Maiha Local Government Council of Adamawa State, Lawan Datti. Reasons unknown.
Unidentified persons kill four, injure nine and virtually destroy a small village in the early morning hours. It is possible the violence was driven by ethnic unrest.
A soldier and 13 members of suspected Boko Haram were killed during a shootout after an explosive was thrown into a military vehicle. Other reports have the death total at 10.

Members of the JTF killed one member of Boko Haram and arrested two others. Following the shootout the JTF recovered 36 large explosives from a den. The deceased was later learned to be an official in the organization.
Soldiers manning a checkpoint in northern Nigeria shot to death two ranking members of Boko Haram, including Abu Qaqa, a spokesman for the group.
Unidentified gunmen shot and killed the justice commissioner, Zannah Malam, in a small town outside of Maiduguri.
Soldiers shoot and kill two suspected Boko Haram commanders on the outskirts of the city.
Unidentified gunmen open fire on two police officers, killing them. along Afikpo Street
Boko Haram gunmen stormed a medical clinic, kill the medical director's son.
Four persons killed following a PDP inter party conflict over a candidate.
Four persons killed following a PDP inter party conflict over a candidate.
The JTF killed four and arrested three suspected members of Boko Haram during two separate raid operations throughout the city.
The JTF conducted two separate Boko Haram raids in different parts of the city. Four dead, three arrested.
The JTF raids a Boko Haram bomb factory, make 156 arrests of suspects, including a high profile leader of the group.

A suspected Boko Haram suicide bomber detonates a car suicide car bomb outside a Catholic Church, at least three killed, plus the bomber, scores injured. Some reports have the death count as high as five.
The Nigerian military kills 35 members of Boko Haram and makes sweeping arrests over two days in three neighborhoods (not named) across the city.
The Nigerian military kills 35 members of Boko Haram and makes sweeping arrests over two days in three neighborhoods (not named) across the city.
One is killed when two armed men entered Lagos State University and opened fire on students. Two others injured.

EVENT_TYPE: Non-violent activity by a conflict actor
NOTES: Military forces arrest 15 members of Boko Haram who had infiltrated security forces as security border agents.
Four people are killed when suspected members of Boko Haram open fire on guests of a wedding. At least one reported injury.
Boko Haram shoot and kill two police officers along a road.

Unidentified gunmen kidnapped the Delta State Commissioner for Higher Education, Prof. Hope Eghagha, assumedly for ransom. During the operation, his orderly, a police sergeant, was killed in the crossfire while his driver reportedly sustained serious injury.
Suspected detonate a suicide style bomb near an Islamic school causing unknown causalities, though injures have been widely reported.
Security agents shot and killed two suspected members of Boko Haram as they attempted to carry out operations on a Christian church following an attack on an Islamic school in the same area.

Gunmen, suspected to Boko Haram, opened fire in a student housing area near a polytechnic school in the northeastern Nigerian city of Mubi, killing at least 40 and injuring at least 15 others. In the following days the death count was raised to 48 and a curfew was imposed. It was later learned the gunmen personally knew their victims, specifically targeting Christians. The following week it was determined by authorities the perpetrators were in face Boko Haram. (Conflicting report: some sources have the attack occurring on 2 Oct, while other have the attack on 1 Oct, still others have differences in the causality count. )
Suspected Boko Haram gunmen shoot and kill 20 at a government housing complex before fleeing ion a boat in the Ngadabul River.
Suspected members of Boko Haram detonate an explosive targeting military patrol, causing one death and four injuries.
Unidentified gunmen shoot and kill two police officers. Boko Haram maintains a presence in the State, but they were not openly suspected here.
An unidentified man (unknown affiliation) detonates a bomb in a heavily populated area of the city, but causes no damage or harm. The individual was later arrested.
JTF forces shoot and kill two suspects in connection to a shooting in a government housing complex which killed twenty.

EVENT_TYPE: Non-violent activity by a conflict actor
NOTES: JTF forces arrest two Boko Haram members in Kaduna State.
Unidentified gunmen shoot and kill two University of Maiduguri students. Authorities are uncertain if it was the work of Boko Haram.
One person is dead and 10 others injured when a explosive detonates in a hotel/ Boko Haram is suspected.

An explosion detonated by unknown persons causes seven causalities, which of whom were brought to a military hospital. Conflicting report: The depot's Public Relations Officer, Capt. Ibrahim Abdullahi, told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Zaria that no death was recorded in the incident.

EVENT_TYPE: Non-violent activity by a conflict actor
NOTES: Police arrest two suspected members of the Boko Haram sect.

Unidentified people attack a Labour Party campaign rally. LP leader publically blame a rival, Action Congress, though this could be a political maneuver. Later in the week it was learned the attackers we're 'cultists.'
Suspected Boko Haram detonate an explosive at a beer garden. Three reported deaths, 12 injuries. Conflicting reports (Xinhua) have one killed, 11 injured.
A explosion near a television station kills a woman and wounded five children. It is unclear who the perpetrators were.
Boko Haram gunmen attack a small town market with firearms, killing three Chinese construction workers an a Nigeria aid.
Boko Haram gunmen clash with JTF members in two separate areas of Damaturu. No deaths reports, several gunmen arrested.
Unknown gunmen have attacked Dogon Kuka village in Yobe State, killing 17. At least two victims died immediately. Authorities will not specify if they believe Boko Haram is a suspect.
Boko Haram gunmen clash with JTF members in two separate areas of Damaturu. No deaths reports, several gunmen arrested.
Unidentified gunmen kidnap the majority leader of the Benus State House assembly, Paul Biam (PDP), and release him 24 hours later. It is unclear if the motive for kidnap was political or criminal.
Mala Kaka, a traditional ruler outspoken against Boko Haram is shot and killed in his home.
JTF members raid a Boko Haram hideout, kill 30, including a senior leader, second-in-command Bakaka, and arrest 11. Conflicting report: some sources claim 31 deaths and 10 arrests.

Suspected Boko Haram (though they did not claim responsibility) detonate a remote controlled explosive near the local headquarters of the Nigeria Union of Journalists. Two passerby soldiers were wounded in the attack when their van drive over the device. Conflicting account: several local residents claim to see six dead taken away by medical units.
Unidentified gunmen attack the official residence of an army commandant, killing at least one member of security personnel.
Unidentified people attack a political headquarters of the PDP as factious members protest party policy.
Two unidentified men assassinate a Enugu State monarch, or traditional ruler, at this shop. Police make several arrests in connection to the murder later in the week.

Two policemen escorting immunization officials were shot dead today by gunmen on motorcycles at Kofar Dawanau area of Kano metropolis. It was later learned Boko Haram was responsible, and arrests were made.

Unknown gunmen yesterday bombed a police station and Unity Bank branch in Gwaram town in Jigawa State with Improvised Explosive Devices (IED). Though the perpetrators were unidentified, Boko Haram has engaged in similar activities in the past.

EVENT_TYPE: Non-violent activity by a conflict actor
NOTES: Police arrest eight suspected members of Boko Haram who they believe are responsible for the shooting deaths of two police officers the previous day.

Unidentified gunmen on motor bikes attacked a Federal Road Safety Commission (FRSC) patrol vehicle, killing two officers and injuring one seriously. The motivation for the violence was not speculated on.
A 75 year-old woman, along with her three children are killed by unknown gunmen. Fulani herdsman were later suspected, and several were arrested in connection with the murders.

Unidentified gunmen kidnap the Rivers State Commissioner for Power, Mr. Augustine Nwokocha, along with his assistant. The perpetrators may have been pirates seeking ransom, witch is common in the area, though the facts are unclear.
A blast, seemingly targeting soldiers, detonates, but causes no causalities. Authorities believe the perpetrators are of Boko Haram.
Four members of a family are killed as they exited a church. Boko Haram is suspected, though authorities cannot determine why this specific group was targeted.

Unknown assailants, disguised as police, attack a mosque in rural Kaduna, as well as the home of a local leader, killing at least 24 people in the pre dawn hours. Some believe the perpetrators were a local band of thieves seeking revenge, others, Boko Haram.
The police detonate an IED after it was discovered by a local opposite a motor park. There were no causalities reported.

At least 15 separate explosions in targeting JTF forces punctuated by gunfire echoed Monday across a Maiduguri city, leaving more than 10 persons dead and telecommunication masts burnt. The explosions started at about 5.15pm and was on intermittently for about 30 minutes and sending serious panic among the people, according to a witness. The violence affected three broad areas.

Witnesses said a gunman suspected to belong to Boko Haram shot dead a police traffic warden in the city within view of a military checkpoint. The gunman simply walked away after the attack unstopped, witnesses said.
